_provenance: Hand-labeled by a Claude subagent from the prose and the Observation alone, before seeing any model's answer, blind to any translator or ground-truth-model output, 2026-09-23.

labels.rationale: Nothing visible and no minion wave to poke — no directive says to hold still, so advance cautiously down the lane.
hp 34/170 (20%) is below the quarter-health line — 'recall the moment you're below a quarter health, no exceptions.'
Enemy is inside melee range (~23 units) — 'you are already losing and should be leaving'; Glissando is the panic-button dash out.

Single enemy ~630 units away, no cluster and no minions — too far for Chord's long range to plausibly reach, and nothing about being 'too close' applies; default to advancing. The exact edge of Chord's range is not given, so this distance judgment is an assumption.
Two enemies plus a minion bunched near self, Chord off cooldown — 'throw it at the densest cluster... the instant it's off cooldown, don't wait for a perfect moment.'
Chord is on cooldown and the enemy isn't in melee range — 'Chord first, basic-attack second, never melee'; with Chord unavailable, basic-attack the visible enemy.

Keytar's prose gives no ally-protection directive at all (unlike drums) and the threat is far across the map — no basis to divert from normal lane behavior; flagged as a place where the prose is simply silent, not just ambiguous.
Chord goes to the densest visible cluster, not the lone enemy — the grouped pair outweighs isolation preference, which is violin's concern, not keytar's.
No bearbot present; poking the tower from range fits the free-damage, no-risk poke ethos, though prose never actually mentions towers — a judgment call.

hp is exactly 25% (42.5/170); 'below a quarter health' read as strictly less-than, so no recall yet at exactly the threshold (ambiguous edge case) — Chord is off cooldown with a visible target, so throw it rather than wait.
The visible minions are own-team wave minions, not an enemy wave to poke, and no enemies are present — continue advancing alongside them.

enemy-close-healthy (~32 units) puts an enemy inside attack/melee range — 'never be the closest thing to an enemy... already losing and should be leaving' — positioning safety takes priority over sniping the far, nearly-dead enemy.
